summary: Wisdom 3 (19 verses) continues the story of faithfulness. Starting with 'But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment will touch them.', it moves through themes of faithfulness, wisdom and calls readers toward hope.
whyItMatters: This chapter matters because it shows faithfulness lived out in second temple period. For a first-time reader, it answers: who is God in this moment, what does he ask, and how do people respond.

keyVerses.text: But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment will touch them.
But the ungodly will be punished even as their reasoning deserves, those who neglected righteousness and revolted from the Lord;
For the end of an unrighteous generation is always grievous.

questions.question: What is happening in Wisdom 3?
questions.answer: In 19 verses, this chapter wisdom 3 (19 verses) continues the story of faithfulness. starting with 'but the souls of the righteous are in the hand of god, and no torment will touch them.', it moves through themes of faithfulness, wisdom and calls readers toward hope. The setting is second temple period, written to jewish community. Look for who speaks, who listens, and what changes by the end.

questions.question: Who wrote Wisdom and why 3 matters in the bigger story?
questions.answer: Traditionally anonymous / tradition, addressed to jewish community around intertestamental. This chapter fits the book's purpose as jewish literature — its themes of faithfulness, wisdom build on what came before.

questions.question: What does 'righteousness' mean in this chapter?
questions.answer: Being in right standing, doing what is right. In this chapter, it appears in context of faithfulness. For a first-time reader: think of it as being in right standing, doing what is right, not just religious jargon.

questions.question: What does this chapter teach about God or people?
questions.answer: Through faithfulness and wisdom, it shows God's character (faithful, just, merciful) and human tendency (need, failure, hope). Notice how verses move from problem to provision.

questions.question: Verse 14 is long — what is it saying in plain English?
questions.answer: The verse says: 'So is the eunuch which has done no lawless deed with his hands, nor imagined wicked things against the Lord; for a precious gift will be given to him for his faithfulness, and a de...' In plain terms: it is making a key point about faithfulness. Break it into two halves — what is described, and what is promised or commanded.

questions.question: How could this chapter apply today without forcing modern ideas onto it?
questions.answer: Ask: what was original audience supposed to do with this? Then ask: what similar situation exists today? For example, if chapter warns about idols, today that might be money or status; if it celebrates deliverance, where do people need deliverance today?
